selection: Tracked projects with coordinates whose public stage is completed, or whose promised handover year (field done in /data/bali-cases.json) is before 2026.

source.name: NASA Black Marble VNP46A2 (VIIRS/NPP Gap-Filled Lunar BRDF-Adjusted Nighttime Lights, daily), via NASA GIBS WMS layer VIIRS_SNPP_GapFilled_BRDF_Corrected_DayNightBand_Radiance
source.license: NASA data, no restrictions on use (NASA Earth Science Data and Information Policy). Please cite Roman et al. 2018, Remote Sensing of Environment.

method: Days 1,8,15,22 of each month for 36 months. Window of 25 x 25 pixels of 15 arc-seconds (about 460 m) on the pin, aligned to the native grid. Pin: mean of the 3 x 3 pixels around the pin. Ring: median of the pixels 4 to 12 pixels away (about 1.9 to 5.5 km). Month: median of its days. Radiance in nW/(cm2 sr) as the midpoint of the GIBS colour bin (0.1 wide at the low end, wider above 2, saturating at 38.2). change_pct: median of the last 12 months against the 12 before, rounded to 5%, only when the earlier level is at least 0.5. pin_vs_ring: last 12 months, only when the ring is at least 0.3. trend_per_year: Theil-Sen slope of the monthly series. Readings: dark if the pin is under 0.5; darker than its surroundings if pin_vs_ring is under 0.5; brighter or dimmer if change_pct is +20% or more, or -20% or less.
limits: Light is a proxy, not proof of occupancy: a finished but empty building can keep its common areas and street lights on, a lived-in villa among trees can look dark, and a construction site with floodlights can look busy. One pixel is about 460 m across, wider than most projects, so neighbours count too. Values are colour bins, not the raw radiance. Gap-filled days repeat the last clear night when it is cloudy. Coordinates are those found in public sources, about 100 m.
